page: Amazon Web Services g7.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, designed for workloads requiring combined graphics rendering, machine learning acceleration, and fast local I/O. The system features 48 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, operating with one thread per core across 48 vCPUs. System memory totals 192.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core allocation.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPUs based on the Blackwell architecture, providing 64 GB of combined video memory. The configuration integrates 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for scratch space and caching, coupled with a 175 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile to prevent data starvation during multi-node transfers or model loading.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, this instance packs a high density of GPU compute, local NVMe capacity, and dedicated host cores into a single package. Workloads that benefit from both high host CPU frequencies and discrete hardware acceleration avoid off-instance bottlenecks, though users must consider that local NVMe storage is ephemeral and complementary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The AWS g7.12xlarge instance fits intensive graphics workloads, 3D spatial rendering, workstation virtualization, mid-scale machine learning model fine-tuning, and high-throughput data pipelines that demand rapid local storage caching alongside GPU execution.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.12xlarge is an accelerated computing server type designed for graphics-intensive and GPU-accelerated computing workloads. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance is powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor delivering 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory at a 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Compute capabilities are bolstered by two NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell GPUs offering 64 GB of total VRAM. High-speed I/O requirements are supported by 1900 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and a 175 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. The high ratio of dedicated physical cores, high-bandwidth networking, and dual Blackwell GPUs makes this instance practical for 3D graphics rendering, computer-aided engineering, workstation virtualization, and machine learning inference pipelines.
